title: Specified-coefficient degree-p quotient component

from.place: Tag 07PR: base change of the binomial presentation

lean.statement:
theorem FormalFiberDegreePQuotient
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (M : IntermediateField K L)
    (F : Type u) [CommRing F] [Algebra K F]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (z : L)
    (hz : IntermediateField.adjoin M ({z} : Set L) = ⊤)
    (a : M) (ha : z ^ p = (a : L)) (hdeg : Module.finrank M L = p) :
    Nonempty ((Polynomial (TensorProduct K M F) ⧸
      Ideal.span ({Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom a)} :
          Set (Polynomial (TensorProduct K M F)))) ≃+* TensorProduct K L F)

statement: Let K be a field, L a field extension of K and M an intermediate field [def-pc-field-extension]. Let F be a commutative K-algebra, p a prime, z in L with M(z)=L, and a in M with z^p=a and [L:M]=p. Put R=M tensor_K F and T=L tensor_K F [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and i(a)=a tensor 1. Then R[Z]/(Z^p-i(a)) [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is isomorphic as a ring to T.

proof.text: The monic polynomial X^p-C(a) vanishes at z, so z is integral. IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank, hz, and finrank_top identify the degree of minpoly M z with p. The minimal polynomial divides the binomial; Polynomial.eq_of_monic_of_dvd_of_natDegree_le therefore identifies them. Compose AdjoinRoot.algEquivOfEq, IntermediateField.adjoinRootEquivAdjoin, IntermediateField.equivOfEq hz, and IntermediateField.topEquiv to obtain the M-algebra equivalence AdjoinRoot (X^p-C(a)) = L.

Apply AdjoinRoot.tensorAlgEquiv directly over K, with left factor F and coefficient ring M. Its result is AdjoinRoot (X^p-C(1 tensor a)) over F tensor_K M. Algebra.TensorProduct.comm K F M and AdjoinRoot.mapRingEquiv transport this to the specified quotient over M tensor_K F, taking 1 tensor a to a tensor 1. Tensor the simple-field equivalence from step 1 with F using Algebra.TensorProduct.congr and restrictScalars K, and finally swap F tensor_K L to L tensor_K F. Compose these ring equivalences. These constructions do not require F to be nonzero.
